title: ShareButton
summary: A share button opens a small panel with the link, a Copy link button and an Email action; where the app has more to offer it hands the link to the Android Sharesheet (an ACTION_SEND intent wrapped in Intent.createChooser) instead. Monarch ships a MonarchPopover for the panel.
whenToUse: To send a link or text to another app or person. Put the intent in the onClick of a MonarchButton, or of an IconButton with a share icon and a content description, inside MonarchTheme.
whenNotToUse: To copy a value to the clipboard use MonarchCopyButton; the Sharesheet already offers Copy, so do not add a copy fallback next to it.
api: Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND).apply { type = "text/plain"; putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TEXT, text); putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TITLE, title) }

options.name: Intent.EXTRA_TEXT
options.description: The link or text to share.

options.name: Intent.EXTRA_TITLE
options.description: A title shown in the preview at the top of the Sharesheet on Android 10 and later.

options.name: Intent.EXTRA_SUBJECT
options.description: A subject that email apps use.

options.name: createChooser title
options.description: Pass null so that the system shows its own localised title.

states.name: resting
states.description: The button that opens the Sharesheet has the states of the button it is: MonarchButton or IconButton.

states.name: sheet open
states.description: The system Sharesheet covers the app; the app is not told which target was chosen unless it passes an IntentSender to createChooser.

appearance: The button follows MonarchTheme like any Monarch button. The Sharesheet is drawn by the system in the system's own colors, not the app theme.
platformNotes: The web component uses the Web Share API where the browser has it and otherwise opens its own panel with the link, a Copy link button and optional targets such as email. Android shows that panel, a MonarchPopover, so the screen reads as on the web; an app that prefers the system chooser puts the ACTION_SEND intent in the onClick of the button instead. iOS uses ShareLink. A web ShareEvent with the chosen target needs a PendingIntent IntentSender on Android; Monarch does not wrap it.
accessibility: System behavior: the Sharesheet is a system screen with its own TalkBack labels and focus order.
The button that opens it is a MonarchButton or an IconButton, so it has the Button role and a touch target of at least 48dp.
An icon-only share button needs a content description such as "Share".
edgeCases: Pass null as the chooser title; a fixed English title would not be translated by the system.
Without Intent.createChooser, Android may open a default app directly; the chooser always shows the Sharesheet.
Share a content:// Uri with FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION and ClipData for files; plain text needs no permission.

examples.title: Share sheet with panel fallback

parityExceptions.reason: The title is the email subject and the title of the system share payload; it is not shown on screen.
parityExceptions.convention: internal values that are not displayed
